steps.title: Check subject–verb agreement
steps.content: The verb must agree with the grammatical subject. Phrases between subject and verb do not usually change the subject's number.
steps.example: Correct: The bouquet of roses is on the table. 'Bouquet' is singular.

steps.title: Find the correct sentence
options: Each of the students have a book.
Each of the students has a book.
Each of students have a book.
steps.explanation: Each is singular, so the verb is has.

steps.title: Check articles and prepositions
steps.content: Use a before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound. Prepositions depend on standard usage and the relationship being expressed.
steps.example: An honest person; a university (the word university begins with a /y/ sound).

steps.title: Spot the tense error
steps.explanation: Present perfect uses has/have + past participle. The past participle of go is gone.

steps.title: Check parallel structure
steps.content: Items in a series should use matching grammatical forms. Also check pronouns for clear references and avoid unnecessary shifts in tense.
steps.example: Parallel: The role requires planning, writing and presenting.

options: Neither of the answers are correct.
Neither of the answers is correct.
questions.explanation: Neither is singular in this construction, so use is.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct article: He waited for ___ hour.
questions.explanation: Hour begins with a vowel sound because h is silent; use an.
News is grammatically singular, so use is.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: By the time we arrived, the show ___.
questions.explanation: Past perfect shows the show began before another past event; begun is the past participle.

options: He enjoys reading, to swim and cycling.
He enjoys read, swim and cycle.
He enjoys reading, swimming and cycling.
He enjoys to reading, swim and cycling.
questions.explanation: All three activities use the same gerund form.
